news.title: Football news: Anthony Gordon urges England to stop trying to replicate Spain
news.lede: Anthony Gordon has made 25 appearances for England and scored four goals. Anthony Gordon says that controlling games is not in the English "DNA" but the Three Lions could win major tournaments if they stop "trying to replicate Spain". The Barcelona winger was speaking at St George's Park as the England squad prepare to take on world champions Spain on Saturday - their first match together since the World Cup. England lost their semi-final 2-1 to Argentina, before beating France 6-4 in the bronze medal match.

news.title: Drunken pub visit to watch World Cup match ends in £785 court bill
news.lede: A MAN'S pub trip to watch World Cup football ended with a £785 court bill after he obstructed police. Police were called to the Newton Grange pub in Newton Hall, Durham, on Wednesday, July 1 after customer Lee Franklin was reported to be behaving in an aggressive manner. Peterlee magistrates heard Franklin was outside when police arrived, and appeared heavily intoxicated and slurring his words. Prosecutor Michael Embleton said officers approached Franklin about an unrelated matter, but he initially ran off, insisting he had done nothing wrong.

news.title: World Cup experience, 22 players abroad: Panama arrive for India friendly
news.lede: Bengaluru: Of the 24 players in Panama’s squad for the friendly against India, 22 ply their trade abroad. Many play in Major League Soccer in the US, while others are competing at an even higher level across Europe and Latin America, including Amir Murillo at Besiktas in Turkey, Andres Andrade at LASK in Austria and Jose Rodriguez at FC Juarez in Mexico.Panama, currently ranked 44th, made their World Cup debut in 2018 and also competed in the last edition won by Spain. They finished runners-up in the 2024-25 CONCACAF Nations League.“. Panama is a country that has a lot of talent,” midfielder Rodriguez told TOI before the visitors took the field for their first training session at the Centre of Sports Excellence here on Wednesday.“.

news.title: ‘Reality check’ for new excitement machines, WC heartbreak star returns to face Brazil
news.lede: The start of a new World Cup cycle for the Socceroos gets underway on Friday night, with Australia taking on five-time world champions Brazil in a two-game series that starts in Townsville before moving to Brisbane on Tuesday. The fixtures come just months after Tony Popovic’s side exited the last World Cup in North America after a heartbreaking penalty shootout loss to Egypt in the Round of 32, and while there are plenty of familiar faces in the squad named by the manager, there’s also a healthy dose of new blood. news.title: Potential debutants called up to star-studded Matildas squad for crucial World Cup prep
news.lede: Three players could make their Matildas debut next month after being named in Australia’s squad for friendly internationals against Germany and Haiti. Uncapped trio Melbourne Victory goalkeeper Courtney Newbon, defender Tori Tumeth (Vancouver Rise, Canada) and midfielder Hana Lowry (Valerenga IF, Norway) could be given game time by Matildas coach Joe Montemurro as he continues to build depth ahead of next year’s FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil. news.title: Harry Kane admits England’s World Cup 2026 exit ‘hurt more than any other’
news.lede: ‘It wasn’t the team that we wanted and said we’d be’. England host Spain in Nations League on Saturday. Harry Kane has described England’s World Cup semi-final defeat against Argentina as his most painful tournament exit because of how the team lost sight of who they were. The captain is determined to move on as quickly as possible and is chasing a statement performance against Spain at Wembley on Saturday night in the Nations League.
